ideas.pitch: A localized, low-latency voice assistant running on edge devices that translates spoken regional queries into exact pesticide and fertilizer measurements.
ideas.problem_statement: A voice assistant that answers a farmer in their own language.
ideas.title: VoiceKisan: Multilingual Offline Voice Assistant for Pesticide Dosage
ideas.why_it_could_win: Judges in the previous edition favored physical or practical implementations like Team Snack Overflow's automated sprinkler; a voice assistant directly tackling vernacular language barriers solves an immediate accessibility problem in rural farming.

ideas.pitch: An autonomous mini-rover utilizing computer vision on a Raspberry Pi to detect localized crop stress and pest infestations, applying pesticides only where needed.
ideas.title: CropShield: Edge AI Rover for Targeted Spot-Spraying
ideas.why_it_could_win: Mirrors the success of past hardware winners by building a working physical prototype that cuts down chemical waste, which instantly appeals to agricultural judges looking for sustainability and hardware grit.

ideas.pitch: An optimized, low-latency plant disease identification model designed to run smoothly on budget smartphones with zero or intermittent internet connectivity.
ideas.title: Niraamaya: Lightweight CNN Plant Disease Classifier for Mobile
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly builds on proven architectures that won contests like CONIA Hackathon 2025 by optimizing CNN inference times for field deployment.

ideas.pitch: An integrated IoT sensor suite and multi-agent diagnostic loop that automatically regulates humidity, drip irrigation, and ventilation inside polyhouses.
ideas.problem_statement: 24 hours. One real farm problem. One room full of people trying to solve it.
ideas.title: PolySense: Automated Polyhouse Climate & Soil Closed-Loop Ops
ideas.why_it_could_win: Combines robust sensor telemetry with automated closed-loop operations, matching the multi-agent diagnostic design that scored high at SEAL Hackathon.

ideas.pitch: A miniature conveyor belt prototype that uses computer vision to grade harvested produce by size, ripeness, and surface blemishes in real time.
ideas.problem_statement: 24 hours. One real farm problem. One room full of people trying to solve it.
ideas.title: AgriSort: Edge-CV Sorting and Grading Conveyor Prototype
ideas.why_it_could_win: A physical, moving mechanical demo always stands out in a crowded exhibition room of software-only web dashboards, matching the crowd-pleasing nature of hardware builds.
